\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{इजाजत} (ijājat)}{इजाजत (ijājat)}]{\mw{इजाजत} (ijājat) — permission}

\label{lesson:MW-C267-ijajat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a petition, then the Marwadi for a blessing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{इजाजत}}
\textbf{\mw{इजाजत}} — \emph{ijājat} — \textquotedblleft{}permission\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{म्हैं} \mw{इजाजत} \mw{ली} \mw{अर} \mw{घरै} \mw{गयो।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mhaĩ ijājat lī ar gharai gayo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I got permission and went home.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{इजाजत}} (\emph{ijājat}) is usually traced, through Persian \emph{ijāzat}, to Arabic \emph{ijāza}, \textquotedblleft{}permission\textquotedblright{}. It is feminine, so \textbf{\mw{म्हैं} \mw{इजाजत} \mw{ली}}, I got permission.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ijājat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ijājat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mhaĩ ijājat lī ar gharai gayo.} — I got permission and went home.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for a petition, then the Marwadi for a blessing, then say \emph{ijājat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{इजाजत} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Permission\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{रजा} (rajā)}{रजा (rajā)}]{\mw{रजा} (rajā) — leave to go}

\label{lesson:MW-C267-raja}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a blessing, then the Marwadi for permission.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{रजा}}
\textbf{\mw{रजा}} — \emph{rajā} — \textquotedblleft{}leave to go\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{हूं} \mw{रजा} \mw{मांगूं} \mw{हूं।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hū̃ rajā māṅgū̃ hū̃.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I ask leave to go.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{रजा}} (\emph{rajā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{riżā}, \textquotedblleft{}consent\textquotedblright{}; asking for it is asking leave to go.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for asking and answering.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{हुकम} (hukam)}{हुकम (hukam)}]{\mw{हुकम} (hukam) — an order}

\label{lesson:MW-C267-hukam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for permission, then the Marwadi for leave to go.

\textbf{\mw{हुकम}} — \emph{hukam} — \textquotedblleft{}an order\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{बाप} \mw{हुकम} \mw{देवै} \mw{है।}

\begin{quote}

A masculine noun.

\textbf{\mw{हुकम}} (\emph{hukam}) is usually traced, through Persian \emph{hukm}, to Arabic \emph{ḥukm}, \textquotedblleft{}judgement, command\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{इंतजार} (intjār)}{इंतजार (intjār)}]{\mw{इंतजार} (intjār) — waiting}

\label{lesson:MW-C267-intjar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for leave to go, then the Marwadi for an order.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{इंतजार}}
\textbf{\mw{इंतजार}} — \emph{intjār} — \textquotedblleft{}waiting\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{हूं} \mw{थारो} \mw{इंतजार} \mw{करूं} \mw{हूं।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hū̃ thāro intjār karū̃ hū̃.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I'm waiting for you.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{इंतजार}} (\emph{intjār}) is usually traced, through Persian \emph{intizār}, to Arabic \emph{intiẓār}, \textquotedblleft{}waiting\textquotedblright{}. The one waited for comes first: \textbf{\mw{थारो} \mw{इंतजार}}, waiting for you.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{थमणो} (thamṇo)}{थमणो (thamṇo)}]{\mw{थमणो} (thamṇo) — to stop; to hold on; to wait}

\label{lesson:MW-C267-thamno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for an order, then the Marwadi for waiting.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{थमणो}}
\textbf{\mw{थमणो}} — \emph{thamṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to stop; to hold on; to wait\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{थोड़ु} \mw{थमो} \mw{सा।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{thoṛu thamo sā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Hold on a moment, please.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \mw{वो} \mw{थम्यो}, \emph{vo thamyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{थमणो}} (\emph{thamṇo}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{stambhate}, \textquotedblleft{}supports, arrests\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry, but lists Sindhi \emph{thamaṇu}, \textquotedblleft{}to stop, subside\textquotedblright{}, Nepali \emph{thāmnu}, \textquotedblleft{}to hold, stop, wait\textquotedblright{}, and Hindi \emph{thāmnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to prop, stop\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13683).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for an order, then the Marwadi for waiting, then say \emph{thamṇo} again
